source.title: Stability Based Generalization Bounds for Exponential Family Langevin Dynamics
source.authors: Arindam Banerjee; Tiancong Chen; Xinyan Li; Yingxue Zhou

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests the effect of partially corrupted labels on CNNs trained with SGLD, a noisy stochastic gradient method, rather than reproducing the original study’s standard training setup.
record.gate_note: The paper itself reports SGLD experiments with label corruption from 0% to 60%. It cites Zhang et al. (2017) for motivation; cited results are not extracted. Other benchmark results do not bear on the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own training-error, convergence and test-error results for a CNN trained with SGLD on 10,000 MNIST examples with 0%–60% label corruption. These bear on V2 and V4 despite the experiments primarily evaluating generalization bounds.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the random-label experiment: training error approaches zero despite corruption, while gradient discrepancy, the generalization bound and empirical test error increase with randomness. The paper's broader conclusion concerns expected-stability bounds for EFLD, their improved sharpness and optimization guarantees.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SGLD, which adds Gaussian noise to stochastic gradients, on a CNN and partially corrupted MNIST labels; the original claim concerns standard deep networks and completely random labels.
record.method_sensitivity: Label-corruption fraction changes the reported training duration and empirical test error.
record.problems: The corruption range stops at 60%; the paper reports qualitative descriptions for the random-label experiment rather than exact error values in the supplied text. The number of epochs required by corruption level is not quantified in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No other results in the paper bear on the listed versions. Figure-only numerical values for Figure 3 are not reconstructed because the supplied text gives no exact values.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling and chance-level test error are not tested. Contrary to the record, unchanged architecture and training settings across the tested corruption levels are documented.
The extra training-time factor is not quantified; the supplied text does not establish monotonic slowing at each successive corruption fraction.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel or Gaussian-input experiments.
Corruption above 60%, the fully random endpoint and approach to chance are not tested; signal learning and noise memorization are not separately measured.
No relevant comparisons of weight decay, dropout or augmentation, or their removal.
No separate trajectories establishing that real-label patterns are learned before noisy labels.

record.verdict_notes: Neither source-original exclusion applies. Remove both proposed limits_scope verdicts: unquantified timing and the untested 60%–100% range do not demonstrate failures or qualifications of the claims.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests corruption only up to 60%, not a completely random labeling; it does not report chance-level test error or whether architecture and hyperparameters remain unchanged relative to true-label training.
It says training takes more epochs with random labels, but does not quantify the time increase or establish a small constant factor.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels and Gaussian-noise inputs are not tested.
Corruption is tested from 0% to 60%, not to all labels being random. The text does not establish that test error rises steadily at every fraction or that remaining signal is captured.
The study does not test whether weight decay, dropout or augmentation prevent fitting random labels, or whether removing them harms true-label generalization.
The study does not compare the order or manner in which real-label patterns and noisy-label memorization are learned.

rows.subject: CNN
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGLD on MNIST while varying the fraction of randomly corrupted labels.
rows.value: For long enough training time, all experiments with different levels of label randomness can achieve almost zero training error.
rows.note: The text reports this result across the tested corruption levels in aggregate; it does not give separate numerical errors for each fraction.
rows.check: Training error alone does not measure V2's convergence cost. Appendix E.3 explicitly specifies the same training settings across corruption levels; Table 5 specifies 1,000 epochs and 30 runs. The architecture is stated in Table 1: two convolutional layers and two fully connected layers.
